lessons.title: -es — the plural your first chapter owed you
lessons.gloss: the plural ending for words that end in a consonant — a rule you have been using since you learned ustedes

segments.text: Say "you," formally. (Usted.) Now say it to a group. (Ustedes.) Hold both of those in your mouth for a moment.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: you have been doing this for fifty chapters

segments.text: Your first chapter gave you half a rule and said the rest was for later. This is later.
A word ending in a vowel adds -s. A word ending in a consonant adds -es.
And you already know the second half, because you have been saying it since the day you learned to address a group:
That is not a special word. That is the consonant rule, and nobody told you. Here it is again on something you also hold:
español becomes españoles — Spanish people, Spanish speakers. los españoles — with the plural article from last chapter.
The extra e is not decoration and not an exception. Try saying usteds out loud. Then españols.
Spanish does not let a word end in that pile of consonants. So when the plural -s would land somewhere unsayable, the language puts in the vowel it needs to get the -s out — and that vowel is e.

Which means the rule is really one rule with a repair attached: add -s; if you cannot say it, make room. That is a better thing to hold than two rules, because it will keep explaining things long after this chapter.

segments.prompt: Which word have you been using this rule on since long before this chapter?

feedback.correct: You had the rule before you had the rule.
feedback.incorrect: Ustedes — that is usted plus the consonant plural.

segments.prompt: Why -es rather than plain -s after a consonant?
acceptedResponses: the bare s would be unsayable
spanish needs a vowel to get the s out

feedback.correct: One rule and a repair, not two rules.
feedback.incorrect: Try saying ustedes without the e. The vowel is there to make the -s pronounceable.

segments.text: Vowel ending — which plural? (-s.) Consonant ending? (-es.) And why? (A bare -s there would be unsayable.) Next: the four articles in one place, now that every one of them has been earned.
